expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: During rollout, old workers, queued jobs, rollback artifacts, or another service can still query the column and fail as soon as the schema changes

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: Split it: deploy the read-removal first... then schedule the drop as a separate explicitly approved migration

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: The irreversible step is DROP COLUMN legacy_email... Proceed only with a verified, tested restore/PITR path

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: Mentions reverting code won't restore data and needing a restore path, but does not describe the rollback scenario

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: Friday is fine only if the destructive step has a tested restore path and an available owner who can execute it

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: No—don't deploy the combined code-and-drop migration this afternoon

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: The irreversible step is DROP COLUMN... deploy the read-removal first [reversible]... hold the column drop
